docs.title: Wildbook to EarthRanger
docs.text:
This connection brings what Wildbook learns about an animal back into the EarthRanger event where the animal was first reported. When an animal in a sighting is identified in Wildbook, the connection writes its name, sex, age, notes and a photo into that animal's row on the EarthRanger event.

It runs through Gundi, so nobody has to copy results from one system to the other by hand.

docs.title: A typical day
docs.text:
1. A ranger records a sighting in EarthRanger. The event has a list with one row per animal seen (for example a herd of giraffes).
  2. The photos are uploaded to Wildbook. Each Wildbook sighting carries a short label in its remarks that points back to the event and the row it came from, such as er=twiga:50325:3 (site twiga, event #50325, row 3).
  3. Researchers match the animals in Wildbook.
  4. A few minutes later, Gundi fills in that row on the EarthRanger event with what Wildbook now knows.

docs.title: What's in scope
docs.text:
From Wildbook Goes into the animal's row in EarthRanger The animal's name (for example HNBF093) The ID field you choose Sex (male, female, unknown) The Sex field you choose Life stage (adult, subadult, juvenile, calf, unknown) The Age field you choose The sighting's remarks Added to the end of the Notes field you choose One photo of the animal The Photo field you choose, if it's empty
  • Every field is optional. You pick which ones to fill in, and the rest of the event stays as it is.
  • It works with any event type that has a list of animals with those fields, for any species.
  • One Wildbook connection can update several EarthRanger sites.
  • Each run leaves a short report in the Gundi portal's activity log: how many rows were updated, how many photos were added, and which sightings were skipped and why.

docs.title: What's out of scope
docs.text:
These are handled elsewhere, or by people:

  • Getting sightings into Wildbook. Uploading photos to Wildbook, and adding the er= label to each sighting, happens outside this connection.
  • Creating EarthRanger events. The connection only updates events that already exist.
  • Matching animals. That is done in Wildbook. A sighting whose animal isn't identified yet waits until it is.
  • Changing anything else on the event, such as its title, location, status, other fields, or rows without a label.
  • Clearing values. The connection fills in and corrects values. It never empties a field.
  • Replacing photos. A row that already has a photo keeps it.
  • Sending EarthRanger edits back to Wildbook. Information flows one way, from Wildbook to EarthRanger.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Ranger
    participant ER as EarthRanger
    participant WB as Wildbook
    actor Researcher
    participant G as Gundi

    Ranger->>ER: Reports a sighting (event #50325, one row per animal)
    Note over ER,WB: Outside this connection
    ER-->>WB: Photos uploaded, each labelled er=twiga:50325:3
    Researcher->>WB: Identifies the animal
    loop Every 20 minutes
        G->>WB: Which labelled sightings changed since last time?
        WB-->>G: Changed sightings, with name, sex, life stage, remarks
        G->>ER: Find event #50325 and read its rows
        G->>WB: Get a photo, if a Photo field is set and the row has none
        G->>ER: Write the new values into row 3
        G->>G: Save where it got to, and log a summary
    end
    Ranger->>ER: Sees the animal's name, sex, age and photo on the event

docs.title: How long it takes
docs.text:
• Gundi checks Wildbook every 20 minutes.
  • It leaves out changes from the last 5 minutes, because Wildbook needs a moment to make them searchable. The next run picks them up.
  • So a change in Wildbook usually shows up in EarthRanger 5 to 25 minutes later.
  • A large batch (for example the first run over months of sightings) can take a few runs to get through. Each run picks up where the last one stopped.
  • The time it takes to upload photos to Wildbook and match the animals isn't part of this, and depends on the people doing that work.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• Setup: what you need in Gundi, Wildbook and EarthRanger, and each setting.
  • Good to know: how values are matched, what gets skipped, and other details worth knowing.

docs.title: The label on each sighting
docs.text:
Gundi finds the EarthRanger row for a Wildbook sighting from a label in the sighting's remarks:

er=<site>:<event number>:<row>
  • Site is the first part of the EarthRanger address: twiga for https://twiga.pamdas.org. It must match the address of the destination in Gundi exactly.
  • Event number is the number EarthRanger shows on the event, such as #50325.
  • Row counts from 1: the third animal in the list is row 3.

The label can sit alongside other remarks, separated by ; or |, for example UNIDENTIFIED; er=twiga:50325:3.

Gundi only looks at sightings labelled for the site it's updating; sightings without a label are never touched. A label it can't read is listed as skipped in the activity log.

docs.title: Wildbook is the source for these fields
docs.text:
• Each time a sighting changes in Wildbook, Gundi writes its current values into the row, even if someone changed that row in EarthRanger in the meantime. Wildbook is treated as the reference for the fields you choose.
  • If someone edits those fields in EarthRanger later, the edit stays until that sighting changes in Wildbook again.
  • If someone edits the event in EarthRanger while Gundi is updating it, Gundi doesn't save over their edit. It tries again on the next run.

docs.title: Only changes are brought across
docs.text: Gundi looks for sightings that changed in Wildbook since its last run. A sighting whose animal isn't identified yet is skipped. When the animal is identified later, that counts as a change, and the next run fills in the row.

docs.title: Start date
docs.text:
• With Start From empty, the first run only marks the starting point, and only Wildbook changes from then on are brought across.
  • To bring across older sightings, set Start From before the first run.
  • Start From only counts for the first run. After that, each run continues from where the last one stopped, so changing the date later has no effect.

docs.title: How values are matched
docs.text:
ID

  • A text field gets the Wildbook name as it is, for example HNBF093.
  • A dropdown gets the choice with that name. A choice that starts with the name followed by a nickname also counts, so HNBF093 picks HNBF093_Aubrey.
  • If two choices could fit, or none does, the field is left as it is.

Sex and Age

These are matched to the dropdown's choices, ignoring capitals, spaces, hyphens and underscores, and accepting common short forms:

Wildbook Matches choices such as male / female / unknown Male, M / Female, F / Unknown, U adult Adult, Ad subadult Subadult, Sub-adult, SA juvenile Juvenile, Juv, Ju calf Calf, Ca
  • If the form has no Juvenile choice, a juvenile in Wildbook goes in as Subadult.
  • If nothing fits, the field is left as it is, and the activity log notes the Wildbook value that had no choice. Adding that choice to the form fixes it for the next change.

Notes

  • The Wildbook remarks are added after the notes already in the row, without the er= label and without the location note added on upload.
  • They're added once. If the row already contains them, nothing changes.
  • The Notes field must be a text field. A dropdown is left alone.

Photo

  • Gundi adds one photo, only when the row's Photo field is empty.
  • With Photo Viewpoint set, only photos whose viewpoint in Wildbook includes that word are used (right also matches frontright). If the animal has none, the row gets no photo.

docs.title: Sightings that are skipped
docs.text:
Each skipped sighting is listed in the activity log with its reason:

Reason in the log What it means the stamp can't be read The remarks have no er= label in the expected form. the stamp is for another site The label points to a different EarthRanger site. the animal isn't identified in Wildbook yet It will be picked up once the animal is matched. event #… not found No single event with that number on the site. event #… has no row … The event's list has fewer rows than the label says. another sighting is stamped for event #… row … Two sightings point to the same row, so only the first is used. event type … has none of the fields That event's type doesn't have the list or the fields set up in Gundi. the event was edited in EarthRanger while updating it It's tried again on the next run.

docs.title: Animals in the background of a photo
docs.text: Wildbook sometimes finds a second animal in the background of a photo and creates an extra sighting for it with the same label. Extra sightings with no sex and no life stage that share a label with another sighting are ignored, so they don't overwrite the row of the animal that was actually reported.

docs.title: Several sites
docs.text:
• One Wildbook connection can update several EarthRanger sites. Add each one as a destination.
  • Each site only receives sightings labelled with its own name, and keeps its own progress.
  • All sites use the same field settings, so their event types need the same field IDs.

docs.title: Keys and tokens
docs.text:
• If the Wildbook key expires or is removed, updates stop and the activity log shows an error. Ask for a new key and paste it into the Authentication settings. The next run continues from where it stopped, so nothing is skipped.
  • If the EarthRanger token in the destination stops working, updates to that site stop in the same way until it's replaced.

docs.title: In Wildbook
docs.text:
• An organization service key (it starts with wbsvc_). Your organization's admin or a Wildbook admin creates it in Wildbook under API Access → Organization service keys. It keeps working until the expiry date Wildbook shows for it, so note that date and ask for a new key before then.
  • The key's account must be able to see the sightings you want to bring across. A Wildbook admin account sees everything. A regular account only sees the records it has access to.
  • The sightings must carry the er= label in their remarks. See The label on each sighting.

Short-lived tokens also work, for testing

A token from API Access → Read data works too, but it expires after a few hours and the updates stop until someone pastes a new one. Use the service key for anything that should keep running.

docs.title: In EarthRanger
docs.text:
• An event type with a list of animals. Each event has a list field (for example Animals or Herd) with one row per animal, and inside each row the fields you want filled in: ID, sex, age, notes and photo, in any combination.
  • The field IDs. For the list and for each field inside it, you need the ID as written in the event type's form, not the label people see. For example the label might be Giraffe ID while the ID is giraffe_id. Your EarthRanger admin can find these in the event type's settings.
  • Dropdown choices that match Wildbook. If Sex or Age is a dropdown, its choices need to match Wildbook's values. See How values are matched.
  • A Photo field must be an attachment field, if you want photos.
  • An EarthRanger user for Gundi that can view and edit events of those types. Its token goes in the EarthRanger destination in Gundi (next section).

docs.title: In Gundi
docs.text:
• An EarthRanger destination for each site to update, with its address and token. If the site already sends or receives data through Gundi, it probably has one.
  • Permission to create connections in your organization in the Gundi portal.

docs.title: Set up the connection
docs.text:
1. In the Gundi portal, add a new connection and choose Wildbook as the provider.
  2. Add your EarthRanger destination (or several) to the connection.
  3. Fill in the Authentication settings and click Test Wildbook Connection.
  4. Fill in the Update EarthRanger Events settings and turn on Run on schedule.
  5. After the next run (up to 20 minutes), open the connection's activity log to see the first report.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Setting What to enter Wildbook Address Your Wildbook's web address as you open it in the browser, for example https://giraffespotter.org. API Token The organization service key (wbsvc_…), or a short-lived Read data token.

docs.title: Update EarthRanger Events
docs.text:
Setting What to enter Run on schedule On, so it checks Wildbook every 20 minutes. List Field The ID of the list that holds one row per animal, for example Herd. Required. ID Field The ID of the field in each row that takes the animal's Wildbook name, for example giraffe_id. Sex Field The ID of the field that takes the animal's sex, for example giraffe_sex. Age Field The ID of the field that takes the animal's life stage, for example giraffe_age. Notes Field The ID of a text field that gets the Wildbook remarks added to it, for example giraffe_notes. Photo Field The ID of an attachment field that gets one photo of the animal, for example giraffe_photo. Photo Viewpoint Only use photos from this side, as Wildbook names it (for example right). Leave empty to take the first photo of any side. Start From Bring across Wildbook changes made on or after this date. Leave empty to start from the first run. See Start date. Test Only: Copies Of Site Leave empty. It's only for test sites that hold copies of another site's events.

Fill in at least one of ID, Sex, Age, Notes or Photo. Leave the others empty to not touch them.

docs.title: Check it's working
docs.text:
The connection's activity log in the Gundi portal shows one entry per site per run, for example:

  • twiga: 12 row(s) updated, 3 photo(s) added, 1 sighting(s) skipped. The entry's details list each change (event, row, field, before and after) and why each skipped sighting was skipped.
  • twiga: no new Wildbook sightings for this site, nothing to update. The run worked and there was nothing new.

An entry with skipped sightings shows as a warning, so it stands out.
